business_problem: Enhancing Lokalee’s customers’ experiences with MongoDB Atlas Search The travel and tourism industry is focused on creating meaningful and memorable experiences.
solution_summary: Enhancing Lokalee’s customers’ experiences with MongoDB Atlas Search The travel and tourism industry is focused on creating meaningful and memorable experiences. Lokalee adopted MongoDB Atlas Search for faster, unified search across 350K+ tickets, enabling efficient filtering and tagging in a single endpoint. “Some hotels are having problems financially because of businesses like Airbnb,” explained Mohamed Daher, Chief Technology Officer at Lokalee. “We use a JavaScript stack, so MongoDB’s NoSQL approach is very easy to work with, especially with the Mongoose library,” said Daher. “We had our tickets in one collection, our venues in another, cities in another, and so on,” explained Daher. “To make the expanded inventory work, we had to run three to five searches on each collection, and it was taking a lot of time.” The result was a risk that buyers would lose patience and drift away to another supplier.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Provides relevance-based text retrieval across Lokalee's documents and application data.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the operational, document, and context data behind Lokalee's AI-powered search and assistant experiences.

data_flow: Business documents, tickets, records, and other operational content stay in MongoDB Atlas Search and MongoDB Atlas, where search indexes or vector embeddings are built and then queried in real time to supply grounded results to applications, assistants, or discovery features. Upstream and downstream integrations include AWS, APIs, big-data pipelines.
business_outcome: Search time cut from 25s to 3–4s 37% increase in sales Easier dev workflows and faster issue resolution
metrics: Searches that once took 20 to 25 seconds, and would even sometimes time-out after 30 seconds, are now completed in three or four seconds.
architecture_clues: Vector search is part of the retrieval layer for semantic or generative-AI use cases.
AI agents or assistants are layered on top of the MongoDB data platform.
The deployment integrates with big-data pipelines.
